speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness, and how long they typically last? Do you notice any rhythmic movements or loss of bladder control?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of head trauma, or have you noticed any triggers like stress or lack of sleep preceding these episodes? I would also like to know if there is a family history of seizures. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG findings and your description of an aura with a muddy taste strongly point to focal seizures originating in the right temporal lobe. To confirm the structural cause and rule out any lesions, I will request a brain MRI. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI confirms this is likely primary focal epilepsy rather than secondary to a structural lesion. Do you have any history of febrile seizures in infancy, and have you started any anti-seizure medication yet?

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a focal seizure with a gustatory aura, post-ictal confusion, and right temporal lobe EEG spikes is classic for temporal lobe epilepsy. Since the MRI is normal, we can rule out structural causes, so I will proceed with the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
